intro: Clinique Nouveau Départ offers a wide range of addiction treatment services for individuals struggling with various types of addictions. These services target both substance and behavioral addictions that include but are not limited to alcohol and drug addictions, gambling, internet and sex addictions, among others. The clinic provides detox, inpatient, outpatient, specialized trauma, and specialized return from relapse programs, each designed to meet specific needs of the clients. The specialized trauma program caters to members of the Canadian armed forces and first responders who experience trauma and stress-related disorders like PTSD. Nursing and medical services are available 24/7 with a maximum of eight people in the program, ensuring individualized attention. The return from relapse program focuses on helping clients overcome challenges they faced in their previous rehabilitation attempts. They learn skills such as emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and mindfulness.

pillars.title: About the Clinic
pillars.body: Located in the Town of Mount Royal on the Island of Montreal, Clinique Nouveau Départ has been providing addiction recovery services for over 30 years. Its mission is to provide hope, reunite families, and improve communities through comprehensive and compassionate care. The clinic has a multidisciplinary team consisting of doctors, psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses, psychotherapists, psychometricians, social workers, and coaches. They offer services in both English and French to ensure all clients can access the services they need. Clinique Nouveau Départ has adequate accommodation facilities, including an executive room, private, semi-private, and triple bedroom options. They also have an entertainment and reading room, fitness room, and laundry room, all aimed at making clients feel comfortable and supported during their recovery journey.

pillars.title: COVID-19 Telehealth Treatment
pillars.body: With the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, Clinique Nouveau Départ has adapted its services to meet the needs of clients seeking addiction treatment. They now offer online telehealth treatment to ensure the continuity of care while keeping clients and staff safe from the virus. This virtual service offers the same quality of personalized attention provided in-person, including assessments, therapy sessions, and individualized treatment plans. The telehealth program benefits include easy and flexible scheduling, convenience, increased accessibility, and affordability.

pillars.title: Aftercare, Alumni and Family Support
pillars.body: Support carries on once the residential stay ends. The centre offers weekly therapy sessions for up to 52 weeks, delivered online through EHN Online, and after that you can keep a monthly check-in for as long as it helps. Former clients can join the alumni program, which holds meetings, activities and special events so people don't face early recovery alone. Families get support during treatment too, and that help is also open to families whose loved one is not a client.

overviewH2: EHN Nouveau Départ Montréal: Centre Overview
overview: Clinique Nouveau Départ – EHN Canada is a reputable addiction rehab center located in Montreal, Quebec. With over three decades of experience in providing specialized services for individuals struggling with addiction and comorbid mental health issues, this private clinic is committed to meeting the unique needs of each patient they serve. Their holistic approach to treatment includes medical, therapeutic, biopsychosocial, and human care.

Their medical care ensures that every patient receives proper diagnosis, assessment, and adequate treatment. Their therapeutic care involves personalized treatment plans that consider factors such as severity of the pathology, social and professional environment, and available support networks. The biopsychosocial component integrates medical, psychiatric, psychological, pharmacological, and therapeutic aspects to provide comprehensive care for the patient. Moreover, the human care approach involves families at every stage of recovery, ensuring that patients receive support not just from medical professionals but also from loved ones.

afterOverview: The centre was listed with us for years as Clinique Nouveau Départ. It now operates as EHN Nouveau Départ Montréal, part of EHN Canada, at the same address in Mont-Royal. It describes itself as a French-speaking centre that serves clients in both official languages, and it holds a permit from Santé et Services sociaux Québec (no. 1104-4989). EHN Canada is accredited with commendation by Agrément Canada under its Qmentum Global program. Treatment here is private pay: residential programs are tax exempt, many private insurance plans cover part of the cost, and financing is available through Medicard.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does EHN Nouveau Départ Montréal cost?
faqs.a: The only prices the centre publishes are for its international residential programs: US$17,000 to US$27,000 for the 28 to 42 day addiction program and US$62,000 for the 63-day trauma and addiction program. Canadian clients get the duration and cost of their program from the client service team after the pre-assessment. The centre says residential programs are tax exempt, and treatment can sometimes be claimed as a medical expense.

The residential program runs for 6 weeks or more, depending on what the assessment recommends. The trauma and addiction program is a 9-week (63-day) stay. The hybrid program is 2 weeks in residence, then 8 weeks of virtual treatment and 12 months of follow-up.

faqs.q: Where is the centre and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The clinic is at 1110 Avenue Beaumont in Mont-Royal (Town of Mount Royal), right across from Acadie metro station on the blue line. Downtown Montreal is about 20 minutes away by car or metro. There is parking beside the clinic, and the building has ramps and elevators.

faqs.q: Are services offered in English or French?
faqs.a: Both. The centre describes itself as French-speaking and says it serves clients in both official languages. It also lists English-language programs through the wider EHN Canada network, so ask admissions which groups would run in your language.

faqs.q: Is this a private centre? Does RAMQ cover it?
faqs.a: It is a private, fee-based centre, separate from the public addiction services run by the CISSS and CIUSSS. The centre does not mention RAMQ coverage. It suggests asking your private insurer whether it covers treatment not funded by the province, and it offers financing through Medicard (iFinance Canada) with terms from 6 months to 7 years.

Aftercare includes weekly therapy sessions for up to 52 weeks, and you can switch to monthly follow-up with no set end date after that. Former clients can also join the alumni program, which runs meetings, activities and special events.

faqs.q: Who can join the trauma program?
faqs.a: The trauma and operational stress program is for members of the Canadian Armed Forces, Veterans Affairs Canada clients, the RCMP and first responders. You join through your care manager, after a phone interview about your substance use and trauma history. Groups are capped at 8 people, with nursing and medical care 24/7.

faqs.q: How long does addiction treatment last at Clinique Nouveau Départ?
faqs.a: The length of treatment depends on the individual needs of each client.

faqs.q: What is the cost of treatment at Clinique Nouveau Départ?
faqs.a: Treatment cost varies depending on the program selected. We accept insurance coverage and offer financing options.

faqs.q: Can I receive addiction treatment while still working?
